name: box_bottom_and_top
note: Fable's case: a 10 mm cube's bottom and top are its height apart, and normally too; met over the whole faces, its witness the pair first by coordinates, (0, 0, 0) to (0, 0, 10). FreeCAD's MeasureDistance reads 10 (its first solution, (0, 10, 0) to (0, 10, 10)). The pinned witness is OCCT's choice, not a hand value: the faces are 10 apart at every pair of points over each other, and which pairs OCCT reports (Silico takes the first of them by coordinates) is OCCT's. It's pinned so a change of it is seen; any of the many would be right, and it's checked on the elements by FreeCAD and against the distance.

name: box_top_and_bottom
note: The same faces the other way round: the witness swaps, nothing else. As for box_bottom_and_top, the witness is OCCT's choice among many, checked on the elements.

name: parallel_faces_apart

name: adjacent_faces_touch
note: Fable's case: the cube's faces x = 0 and y = 0 share an edge: 0 apart; at 90 degrees, so no normal distance.

name: faces_a_nanometre_apart

name: parallel_edges

The pinned witness is OCCT's choice, not a hand value: the edges are 2 apart all along them, and which pairs OCCT reports is OCCT's. The pinned witness is OCCT's choice between the two pairs, not a hand value (either is right); it's pinned so a change of it is seen, and checked on the elements by FreeCAD and against the distance.

name: opposite_quarter_arcs_swapped
